57312.description:
This is our beloved Fender Pawn Shop... Mr Ramparte. Despite these things being pretty cheap on the used market, they're pretty sought after and rare these days. In our opinion, some of the best sounding amps fender has ever put out and we use this fella for MOST if not ALL recording sessions since we got it. Tonnes of personality and super fun.

No nonsense controls. Two channels: Cool and Hot as well as corresponding volumes... that's IT. 

Mic'd with a classic combination of SM57 and R-121 with the ability to hear them summed together. As ever for the Blue Bell Hill Studios Collection, the amp runs through our early 1987 SSL G console which was used to record and mix Busted, McFly, Raye, Sam Fender, Jungle, Arctic Monkeys and Kasabian amongst many others through the years. For more information on the studio, be sure to check out the website.

The Holy Grail... This is a beautiful JMI-era, 1965 Vox AC30 twin with 6 inputs (Brilliant, Normal and Vib-Trem, all with high and low sensitivity) AND the top boost circuitry on the brilliant channel. JMI era too which, for those that don't know, was the glory days for Vox, where they were built in Essex, UK and were built for the standards of all the most iconic bands of the time. One of the big 3 names and the amp that gave them that status.

Whilst in person these vintage AC30s can absolutely take your head off and are very difficult to tame. The sweet spot (captured here) is uncomfortable to sit in front of in a normal sized room... But under a microphone through a vintage console... Oh my god. This particular amp is loaded with vintage Celestion alnico blue speakers that absolutely impart their character in boatloads, unlike the modern recreations which are much tamer. Expect pure vintage tone from this amp that is unmistakably one of the most expensive and sought after tones of all time. 

Of course, This was captured using our Neve 1073 preamps, summed using our SSL 6000G console at Blue Bell Hill Studios. The amp will be available for purchase from Vintage Amporium if you'd like to own the real thing and a piece of rock and roll history for a fantastic price... Link below!

66547.description:
THIS is the real deal. The rarest iteration of the AC50, famously a collaborative effort between Vox and The Beatles (if which this may be one of theirs but more on that in a video we'll be making soon so follow to keep up to date on that!). This is basically a top boost AC30 circuit, tube rectified but with two very notable changes: first of all, a pair of EL34s as opposed to the more commonly associated EL84s seen in most Vox-style amps. This was in order to achieve more headroom (closer to a clean 40W). Secondly, the ECC82 / 12AU7 as opposed to the raunchier ECC83s / 12AX7s seen in most amplifiers these days. This gives the amplifier a brutally clean tone all the way up to the 3 o'clock position on the volume knob. 

This head has been paired with a faithful recreation of its matching cabinet from the glory days... 2 celestion alnico blues, paired with a midax horn. The horn was added as players complained that the AC50 was too dark sounding and wasn't cutting through live. This gave Vox the idea to chuck a horn in which would handle those upper mids' harmonics as well as to stop the 15W blues from getting overloaded by the immense wattage coming from the head.

Of course, This was captured using our Neve 1073 preamps, summed using our SSL 6000G console at Blue Bell Hill Studios. Though as opposed to the more common SM57 and R121, I found that this wasn't taking in much of that midax horn and thus was sounding a little dark. Therefore, I decided to close mic the blue speakers with a typical SM57 and used our Coles as a somewhat far mic (around a foot or so away from the cabinet and positioned low) to take in a more true-to-life version of the amplifier and how it sounds in person. The result, a break up that screams Helter Skelter and a clean that reminds us of the swinging 60s. 84556.description:
THIS is the infamous Fender Bassman 5F6-A. Known for being the circuit from which Marshall was birthed and this particular example has been toured with Clapton himself during the 90s, it even has the stage settings marked out from the 1998 / 1999 Pilgrim Tour... if you've always wanted that Clapton tone and you've got the guitar, THIS is your holy grail.

This amplifier is the epitome of loud blues rock tones and pairs perfectly with a Stratocaster or Les Paul type guitar. We had the amplifier for so little time that by the point I was ready to offer the seller some cash - somebody else had just called in and bought it! The speakers from what we can tell are original 4x10 blue back speakers and features Groove tube power valves and a Mullard GZ34 rectifier tube. Unfortunately, though we had suspected otherwise, the amplifier was not modded by Mr. Dumble as we're told all of Eric Clapton's amps were. The amp came directly from Clapton's right hand man for the Pilgrim tour, the late Alan Darby - though he stood to the left of Eric!

The amplifier has been captured at FULL VOLUME (I went deaf for about 30 minutes after we'd finished this one) in the live room at Blue Bell Hill Studios in Kent, UK using a classic pairing of Shure SM57 and Royer R121 into the gorgeous 1987 SSL 6000G console there used to mix and record countless hit records and summed at a perfect phase alignment for the best representation of each tone we found.

This amplifier is apart of our Music Locker collaboration and as such if you're interested in buying some beautiful rare and vintage gear, check out the original listing on their website linked below.
